title: Inquest into man's death results in six recommendations
subtitle: A coroner's inquest into the death of a homeless Hamilton man in 2006 has resulted in a number of recommendations for the police force and the Ontario Police College.
article: A coroner's inquest into the death of a homeless Hamilton man in 2006 has resulted in a number of recommendations for the police force and the Ontario Police College.

The inquest, which started Monday and lasted three days, was centred on the death of Darin Fournier, a 40-year-old who died from blunt force trauma to the head following a fall while in police custody.
According to the office of the chief coroner, the five-member jury made six recommendations.
The jury asked primarily for more review of custody care policies by Hamilton police officers and that the Fournier death be used as a case study at the Ontario Police College.

Fournier died on Feb. 12 in hospital from an injury he suffered three days prior at the police Central Station. He had been pickup by officers outside the LCBO on Dundurn Street South for public intoxication.

According to Sheila Fournier, Darin's sister who attended the inquest this week, officers said her brother was very drunk and became "difficult" while in custody and started a fight. He fell back and struck his head on the floor but a Special Investigations Unit report says he did not show any sign of external injury.
Fournier was unresponsive when officers tried to rouse him hours later and he was transported to hospital. He died three days later.
An autopsy revealed he died from bleeding in his brain.

The province's police watchdog, SIU, cleared the officers of any wrongdoing a few months later after it was concluded Fournier instigated the struggle and police did not intentionally cause him to fall.
Sheila said the family is happy with the recommendations made by the jury but found it tough to sit through again.
"It was like reliving it all over again," she said today. "This feels like it's never ending."
